pass: A pass is one loop review of the queue that records the actions chosen for its items.
hold: A hold leaves an item waiting because its recorded condition does not yet allow the next step.
hold-only pass: A hold-only pass is a queue review in which every recorded action left work waiting and nothing moved.
action: An action is the next operation the loop chose for an item, such as dispatch, judge, settle, or hold.
lane: A lane is an isolated working directory assigned to one piece of work at a time.
run: A run is one recorded attempt by an agent to work on an item in a lane.
candidate: A candidate is a committed result from a run that can be checked for landing.
gate: A gate is the set of checks that judges whether a candidate is safe to land.
landing: A landing is the recorded application of an accepted candidate to the repository's shared branch.
heartbeat: A heartbeat is the loop's periodically refreshed record showing that its process is still alive.
session: A session is one loop process lifetime, recorded from its start through its last heartbeat and stop.
